data.name: Haribala
data.gender_notes: Haribala is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Haribala is a name derived from Sanskrit where Hari represents Lord Vishnu, the preserver of the universe, and Bala refers to strength. It signifies the divine protection and strength that one derives from the deity Vishnu. The name Haribala carries the meaning “Hari (God Vishnu) + Bala (Strength)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Haribala usually hope their child will grow to embody hari (god vishnu) + bala (strength) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Divine strength and protection from Lord Vishnu
data.etymology: Haribala belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Hari (God Vishnu) + Bala (Strength).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Haribala total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

In Hinduism, names often reflect the divine influences that shape an individual's life. Haribala's name also suggests an association with Lord Vishnu, who is revered for his protective and sustaining qualities. Thus, it carries a rich cultural heritage and represents the spiritual values cherished by millions of Hindus around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Haribala holds immense spiritual significance as it provides a constant reminder of the underlying power and protection that comes from connecting with the divine. The name signifies the belief that one can find strength in Lord Vishnu, who is considered an embodiment of compassion, love, and wisdom. historical_references.reference: Haribala was an influential Vaishnavite poet and philosopher of the Bengal region in the late 16th and early 17th centuries. He wrote extensively on the themes of devotion to Vishnu and the importance of inner spiritual transformation. His most famous work, 'Haribhakti Vilasa', is a comprehensive guide to the practice of Bhakti yoga.
historical_references.context: Vaishnavite poet and philosopher in Bengal

historical_references.reference: Haribala, also known as Haridas Thakur, was a prominent figure in the Chaitanya Charitamrita, a seminal work on the life and teachings of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, a major figure in the Bengal renaissance of Hinduism in the 16th century. Haribala was a devoted follower of Chaitanya and played a significant role in spreading his teachings throughout Bengal and beyond.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Haribala continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
